A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring applies; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. item.problem_title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
item.problem_statement: Estimating a per-protocol effect requires the sustained strategy and its relevant treatment versions to be clinically specified first; artificial censoring with inverse probability weighting is one valid estimation route rather than a requirement. Beneath the mechanics sits the question the mechanics assume answered: what counts as the same treatment. Real treatments differ by dose, route, provider, formulation, combination and adherence pattern, and two regimens sharing a label may not satisfy consistency. Clone-censor-weight handles a patient compatible with several predefined strategies and does not decide whether versions should be pooled into one. Observed data can expose heterogeneity across versions and cannot establish that versions are irrelevant, so the pooling decision is clinical. item.problem_title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
item.problem_statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from observed data. Neither, strictly, can positivity, model correctness or phenotype validity: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them. Current reports blur both distinctions. A propensity-score overlap plot is offered and the reader infers that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot is a partial diagnostic of one of them and silent on the rest. No standard panel exists, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and an absent diagnostic cannot be distinguished from one that was run and not reported. A single panel cannot be adequate for every design, which is a constraint on the solution rather than an argument against it.

item.problem_title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
item.problem_statement: Three trials are in play in any emulation and only one is usually named: the ideal trial that would answer the decision-maker's question, the target trial the investigator specifies, and the emulation the data support. Specifying the target trial closely around the available data conceals the distance between the first two, and the paper reports one estimate as though the chain were tight. What is missing is not an additive decomposition; that generally does not exist, because the transitions change populations, interventions, outcomes and scales, so the discrepancies do not add. What is missing is a documented lineage: the change from the decision question to the operational causal estimand, the assumptions mapping that estimand to an observed-data functional, and the estimation uncertainty, each recorded separately so a reader can see which step carries the load. item.problem_title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
item.problem_statement: Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can fail precisely because the recording is itself informative, last observation carried forward constructs a history in which the absence of measurement was itself evidence, and conditioning on having been observed can induce selection bias. Three estimator families now address this: multiply robust estimation under covariate-driven observation times, calibrated inverse probability weights under irregular visits, and continuous-time weights built from a marked point process. item.problem_title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
item.problem_statement: A successful replication calibrates one emulation of one trial in one database. Transferring that confidence to a different question, or to the same question in a different database, is not an inference the benchmarking design licenses: it requires a target performance estimand stated in advance, an explicit selection or transport model, conditional exchangeability across the questions being compared, and overlap in whatever modifies emulation quality. Outside that support the transfer is model-dependent rather than identified, and frameworks that have been proposed for it remain unevaluated in that role. The benchmarking corpus is also a selected sample: trials get emulated when they are recent, large and have an accessible active comparator, which are the conditions under which emulation works best. item.problem_title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
item.problem_statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail. Truncation is bias-variance regularization: it cannot identify an effect where the treatment density is structurally zero, and a marginal weight summary does not say which intervention-relevant histories carry small or zero density. What a reader needs and does not get is a policy-specific support criterion fixed in advance, diagnostics localized by time and by history, the fraction of the target population that fails the criterion, and the estimand that survives once those strata are set aside. Empirically, poor overlap has been shown to defeat adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure a weight histogram is least able to show. Software
item.paper: The importance of the design of observational studies in comparative effectiveness research: Lessons from the GARFIELD-AF and ORBIT-AF registries.
item.evidence: A tabular scan for empty cells arising from unusual covariate combinations is a real positivity diagnostic that names covariate strata rather than summarizing weights, and it is executed in both registries. What is reported downstream is still weight behavior: mean 1.99 with maximum 39.18 in GARFIELD-AF, mean 2.03 with maximum 57.21 in ORBIT-AF, and hazard ratios at four truncation levels. No unsupported patient history is named, and no rule says at what weight or what empty-cell count the comparison should not be made.
